tagline: The library npm uses to read, compare and match version numbers like 1.2.3 and ranges like ^1.2.0.

source.note: semver v7.7.3, unchanged except one line in ranges/subset.js (line 233, in higherGT: the two operators swapped) so that real tests fail.

districts.classes: The three core types: SemVer (one version), Comparator (one condition like >=1.2.0) and Range (a whole range made of comparators).
districts.functions: Small helpers that work on single versions: parse, clean, compare, sort, bump with inc, and diff, which names the kind of change between two versions.
districts.ranges: Helpers that work on ranges: is a version inside or outside a range, the lowest or highest match, and whether two ranges overlap.
districts.internal: Plumbing shared by everything else: the big regular expressions, constants and limits, option parsing, a tiny cache and debug logging.
districts.root: The front door: index.js gathers every class and helper into the one object you get from require('semver').

buildings.index.js: Collects every class and helper into the single object that require('semver') returns.
buildings.classes/index.js: Exports the SemVer, Range and Comparator classes together.
buildings.classes/semver.js: The SemVer class: parses one version into major, minor, patch, prerelease and build, compares two versions and bumps them.
buildings.classes/comparator.js: One condition such as >=1.2.0: parses it, tests a version against it and checks if two conditions can overlap.
buildings.classes/range.js: Turns range text like ^1.2 || ~2.0 into sets of comparators, expanding tildes, carets, x-ranges and hyphens, and tests versions.
buildings.functions/clean.js: Strips spaces and a leading = or v from a version string and returns the clean version, or null.
buildings.functions/cmp.js: Compares two versions with an operator given as text, like '>=' or '!==', by calling the matching helper.
buildings.functions/coerce.js: Pulls something version-like out of messy text, so 'v2' or 'release 1.4.7.1' becomes a proper version.
buildings.functions/compare-build.js: Compares two versions and, when they are equal, breaks the tie using their build metadata.
buildings.functions/compare-loose.js: Compares two versions in loose mode, which forgives some sloppy formatting.
buildings.functions/compare.js: Returns -1, 0 or 1 for two versions; most other comparison helpers are built on this one.
buildings.functions/diff.js: Says what kind of change separates two versions: major, minor, patch, a pre- variant, or null if they are equal.
buildings.functions/eq.js: True when two versions are equal.
buildings.functions/gt.js: True when the first version is greater than the second.
buildings.functions/gte.js: True when the first version is greater than or equal to the second.
buildings.functions/inc.js: Returns the next version for a release type like major, minor, patch or prerelease, or null if it cannot.
buildings.functions/lt.js: True when the first version is less than the second.
buildings.functions/lte.js: True when the first version is less than or equal to the second.
buildings.functions/major.js: Returns the major number of a version.
buildings.functions/minor.js: Returns the minor number of a version.
buildings.functions/neq.js: True when two versions are not equal.
buildings.functions/parse.js: Turns a string into a SemVer object, returning null (or throwing, if asked) when it is not a valid version.
buildings.functions/patch.js: Returns the patch number of a version.
buildings.functions/prerelease.js: Returns the prerelease parts of a version, like ['beta', 1], or null when there are none.
buildings.functions/rcompare.js: Compares two versions in reverse order, handy for sorting newest first.
buildings.functions/rsort.js: Sorts a list of versions from newest to oldest.
buildings.functions/satisfies.js: True when a version falls inside a range; false if the range itself is invalid.
buildings.functions/sort.js: Sorts a list of versions from oldest to newest.
buildings.functions/valid.js: Returns the normalised version string if the input is valid, otherwise null.
buildings.ranges/gtr.js: True when a version is higher than every version the range allows.
buildings.ranges/intersects.js: True when two ranges share at least one possible version.
buildings.ranges/ltr.js: True when a version is lower than every version the range allows.
buildings.ranges/max-satisfying.js: Picks the highest version from a list that fits a range.
buildings.ranges/min-satisfying.js: Picks the lowest version from a list that fits a range.
buildings.ranges/min-version.js: Works out the lowest version that could ever satisfy a range.
buildings.ranges/outside.js: Shared logic for gtr and ltr: checks whether a version sits entirely above or below a range.
buildings.ranges/simplify.js: Given a list of versions and a range, writes a shorter range that matches the same versions.
buildings.ranges/subset.js: Decides whether every version one range allows is also allowed by another, using helpers that pick the tighter lower and upper bounds.
buildings.ranges/to-comparators.js: Breaks a range into plain lists of comparator strings, mostly for tests and old callers.
buildings.ranges/valid.js: Returns the normalised range string if the range is valid, otherwise null.
buildings.internal/constants.js: Shared limits and names: max version length, the safe integer limit and the list of release types.
buildings.internal/debug.js: Prints debug lines to stderr only when NODE_DEBUG includes semver; otherwise does nothing.
buildings.internal/identifiers.js: Compares prerelease identifiers, treating numbers as numbers and everything else as text.
buildings.internal/lrucache.js: A tiny least-recently-used cache, so parsing the same range twice is fast.
buildings.internal/parse-options.js: Normalises the options argument, so true or {loose: true} both mean loose mode.
buildings.internal/re.js: Builds every regular expression semver uses, plus safer copies that avoid slow pathological matches.

guide.intro: This is semver, the code npm uses to understand version numbers. Each building is a file, each floor a function. One building is on fire: a real test is failing.
guide.onFire: {file} is burning, in {fn}. {failed} checks fail: it now thinks >2.0.0 is looser than >=2.0.0, so subset answers wrongly for ranges with the same lower version.
guide.done: All {total} checks pass again. Two operators in {fn} went back to their places and the fire is out.

fix.explanation: When two lower bounds share a version, higherGT must keep >X over >=X because it is stricter. The bug swapped the operators, so it kept >=X and subset gave wrong answers.
